title: Keycloak OIDC Login and Token Validation
summary: A browser logs in via Keycloak using the authorization code flow, then the app and gateway validate the resulting JWTs.

nodes.label: Browser
nodes.detail: Redirected to Keycloak for login and returns with an authorization code.

nodes.label: App (OIDC Client)
nodes.detail: Registered as a client in a realm. Exchanges the authorization code for tokens, using PKCE for public clients.

nodes.label: Keycloak Realm
nodes.detail: A realm isolates users, clients, roles and settings. Authenticates users and issues ID, access and refresh tokens.

nodes.label: Login Flow
nodes.detail: Authentication flows can require password, OTP or WebAuthn, and run required actions before issuing a code.

nodes.label: User Store
nodes.detail: Keycloak persists realm configuration and users in a relational database, or federates to LDAP or Active Directory.

nodes.label: JWKS Endpoint
nodes.detail: Publishes realm public keys so resource servers can verify token signatures without calling Keycloak per request.

nodes.label: API Gateway
nodes.detail: Verifies signature, issuer, audience and expiry of the bearer token, then forwards allowed requests.

nodes.label: Resource API
nodes.detail: Authorises using claims such as roles or scopes from the validated token.

steps.title: App redirects to Keycloak
steps.text: An unauthenticated user is sent to the realm's authorization endpoint with client ID and PKCE challenge.

steps.title: User authenticates
steps.text: Keycloak runs the login flow, checking credentials against its user store and any MFA step.

steps.title: Code returns, tokens issued
steps.text: The browser returns with a code; the app exchanges it for access, ID and refresh tokens.

steps.title: Calls carry the access token
steps.text: The client calls the API with a bearer token in the Authorization header.

steps.title: Gateway validates the JWT
steps.text: Using cached JWKS keys it checks signature, issuer, audience and expiry, then forwards.
